\section{Overview}

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Limiting majority Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b001
}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.arcsinOddPowerCoefficient}
For each natural number $k$, the limiting majority Fourier weight is $\frac{2}{\pi}$
times the coefficient of the odd power $x^{2k+1}$ in the power series of $\arcsin x$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $k$, the limiting majority Fourier weight is $\frac{4}{\pi k
2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$ when $k$ is odd, and is $0$ when $k$ is even.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Tail of the limiting Fourier weights]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b002
}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight}
For each natural number $k$, define the tail sum of the limiting majority Fourier
weights by summing the weight at every natural number $j>k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Summability of the majority weights]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_summable}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeightAbove_summable}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_hasSum_one}
\difficulty{2}
For every natural number $k$, the limiting majority Fourier weights indexed by natural
numbers $j>k$ form a summable series.
\end{theorem}
